counterevidence_considered.description: Strongest fact potentially supporting the in-scope issue: flare detection (the numerator measurement) was performed only on the 32 retained light curves, so the measurement process itself covers only the retained subset. However, the report keeps all 40 planned units in the denominator, counts unassessable stars as non-events, and explicitly labels the result a lower bound for the planned set — so the retained-subset measurement is not substituted for the complete-domain rate; the reported number is genuinely an events-per-planned-unit quantity.
counterevidence_considered.observed_value: numerator assessed on retained stars only, with disclosed lower-bound treatment

extensions.x-stage1-falsification-attempt: I attempted to demonstrate the issue by checking whether any retained-subset quantity is presented under a complete-domain label. The selected result's value 0.3000 equals 12/40, not the retained-subset value 12/32 = 0.3750, so no subset rate is relabeled; the workflow confirms denominator = planned. I then tested the converse concern — that assessing flares only on retained stars could smuggle a subset-scoped estimate into a complete-set claim — but the report explicitly discloses that removed stars are counted as non-events and bounds the claim as a lower limit, and it claims no separate retained-subset rate. Finally, I recomputed all counts from inputs/data.csv and found them consistent with the report. No path to a demonstrated instance of the in-scope issue class succeeded.
